title: debug - b12628f3
description:
Looking at the error, the core issue is that the model is overfitting severely — training loss drops to near-zero while validation loss increases, and the validation log-loss is NaN (infinity). This happens because:

1. The model's classifier head is randomly initialized (newly initialized weights warning) and needs proper training
2. The small batch size with gradient accumulation and `drop_last=True` causes inconsistent gradient updates
3. No feature engineering is used to provide additional signals

The fix strategy: Switch to a simpler, more robust approach using TF-IDF features with a calibrated classifier (like LogisticRegression or LightGBM) instead of the ModernBERT sequence classifier which is overfitting catastrophically on this small dataset. This ensures stable, well-calibrated probability outputs.
method: The solution uses TF-IDF vectorization (with 1-3 n-grams, up to 50k features) combined with manually engineered statistical features (character/word/sentence counts, punctuation counts, quote density, capital ratio, unique word ratio, stopword ratio) to classify text by author. Features are scaled with StandardScaler and combined via sparse matrix hstack. A multinomial Logistic Regression model (C=4.0, solver='saga') is trained using 5-fold StratifiedKFold cross-validation. The evaluation metric is log loss, and predictions are averaged across folds then normalized to produce the final submission.
